pl-l4d35c4-d1e115.summary: Asks whether one may marry a woman previously defiled by adultery.

pl-l4d35c4-d1e118.summary: Cites Pope Leo: no one may marry the woman he previously defiled by adultery.
claims: Marrying one's adulterous partner is forbidden.

pl-l4d35c4-d1e124.summary: Adds a ruling: someone violated another's wife and swore to the adulteress that if he survived her husband he would marry her, which he did; such marriage we forbid and anathematize.
claims: A promise of marriage during adultery bars that marriage.

pl-l4d35c4-d1e131.summary: Notes that these and other authorities forbid those who defiled themselves by adultery to marry.

pl-l4d35c4-d1e134.summary: Gives Augustine to the contrary: after the death of the one with whom there was true marriage, marriage can be made with her with whom adultery preceded.
claims: Augustine allows such marriage after the spouse's death.

pl-l4d35c4-d1e143.summary: Adds Augustine: it is clear that lawful marriage can be made from persons unlawfully joined, if an honest agreement follows.
claims: Unlawful unions can become lawful marriages.

pl-l4d35c4-d1e149.summary: Interprets this last authority as concerning concubines, who can pass to the honest agreement of marriage if willing to keep chastity and faith.

pl-l4d35c4-d1e152.summary: Interprets Augustine's first authority as concerning those who repented and plotted nothing against the husband's life, nor, while he lived, did the adulterer promise the adulteress to marry her if he survived; those who did are forbidden by the other authorities.
claims: Penitent adulterers who neither plotted nor promised may marry.

pl-l4d35c4.summary: Asks whether one may marry a woman previously defiled by adultery. Leo and a council forbid marrying one previously defiled by adultery, especially when the adulterer swore to marry her after her husband's death. Augustine says marriage can follow adultery after the true spouse dies, and lawful marriage can arise from unlawful union by honest agreement. Lombard reconciles: the latter concerns concubines who adopt marital faith, and those who repented and neither plotted the husband's death nor promised marriage during his life; those who did so are forbidden.
claims: Those who plotted or promised marriage during adultery may not marry.
Penitent adulterers who did not plot may marry after the spouse's death.
Concubinage may become lawful marriage by honest agreement.
